:::{#exm-hyperplane-graph}
#### The graph of a line is a line in the plane

Take $p = 1$, $\vw = 2$, $b = 1$.
The [graph](functions.qmd#def-graph) of $y = 2x + 1$ is the [set](sets.qmd#def-set) of points $(x, y)$ in $\reals^2$ with $2x - y + 1 = 0$.
By @thm-hyperplane-graph, this is a [hyperplane](linear-algebra-matrices.qmd#def-hyperplane) with [normal vector](linear-algebra-matrices.qmd#def-normal-vector) $(2, -1)$.
The point $(0, 1)$ is on it,
since $2 \cdot 0 - 1 + 1 = 0$.
The point $(0, 0)$ is off it,
since $2 \cdot 0 - 0 + 1 = 1 \ne 0$.
@fig-hyperplane-graph shows the line, the two points, and the normal vector drawn from $(0, 1)$.

```{r}
#| label: fig-hyperplane-graph
#| fig-cap: >-
#|   The graph of $y = 2x + 1$, a line in the plane,
#|   with its normal vector $(2, -1)$ drawn from the point $(0, 1)$ on it
#|   and the point $(0, 0)$ off it
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   A straight line rising to the right through the point (0, 1).
#|   An arrow from (0, 1) points right and down, perpendicular to the line.
#|   A second point at the origin lies below the line.
normal_arrow <- grid::arrow(length = grid::unit(0.15, "inches"))
points <- data.frame(x = c(0, 0), y = c(1, 0), label = c("on the line", "off the line"))
ggplot2::ggplot() +
  ggplot2::geom_abline(intercept = 1, slope = 2) +
  ggplot2::geom_segment(
    ggplot2::aes(x = 0, y = 1, xend = 2, yend = 0),
    arrow = normal_arrow
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(ggplot2::aes(x = x, y = y, colour = label), data = points, size = 3) +
  ggplot2::coord_fixed(xlim = c(-2, 3), ylim = c(-2, 4)) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "x", y = "y", colour = NULL)
```

:::
